item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #3 — Decoder: Tariffs didn’t bring manufacturing jobs back to the US
item.content:encoded:
Score: 74/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

The episode delivers strategic analysis of global trade, tariffs, AI, and manufacturing, featuring a CEO with firsthand experience. It is highly relevant for product leaders navigating international supply chains and emerging tech.

Summary

Evan Smith, CEO of Altana, discusses the real-world impact of tariffs on global manufacturing and trade, revealing that protectionist policies have not brought jobs back to the US. The conversation covers the chaos of international relations, agentic AI's role in supply chains, and how geopolitical instability affects product and business strategy. Smith provides operator-level insights into navigating complex regulatory environments, adapting to shifting trade policies, and leveraging AI for resilience. The episode is rich in strategic lessons for leaders managing global eCommerce, supply chains, and technology-driven operations.

Key Ideas

  • Tariffs failed to restore US manufacturing jobs; global supply chains remain complex.
  • Agentic AI as a tool for supply chain adaptation and resilience.
  • Geopolitical instability (Iran, Southeast Asia) directly impacts business strategy.

Implications

Senior product leaders must understand the limitations of policy-driven supply chain shifts, invest in AI for operational agility, and monitor geopolitical risks. Strategic decisions should be informed by real-world trade dynamics and emerging tech.
